From: Veridian AI Compliance <compliance@veridian.ai>

Subject: Data residency confirmation + PrivateLink details for EU pilot

Hi Sean,

Thanks for taking the call earlier — quick follow up from Veridian's compliance team. We're preparing our SIG/CAIQ review and need a concise set of artifacts to validate EU-only hosting for our pilot. Can you confirm the following and share any supporting files: 

- A short statement confirming that customer-controlled VPC private deployments in the EU region will not egress traffic outside EU boundaries (we need network routing assurances).
- A PrivateLink/privatenet topology diagram showing where traffic terminates and how egress is controlled for the EU deployment.
- A CAIQ subset indicating deployment boundary answers (network, encryption at rest, key management partitioning).
- SOC 2 artifact pointers (or a path to restricted access in the dataroom) for encryption and change control evidence.
- Clarification on ephemeral key lifecycle for KV caches and whether keystore separation is applied per-customer for Dedicated/Private installs.

We have an internal deadline to sign the MPA and start onboarding the EU pilot the week of Oct 19. If you can provide the attachments or a plan to hand them over by Oct 16 that will keep us on track.

Thanks,
Oliver Grant
Compliance Program Manager
Veridian AI

Subject: Re: Data residency confirmation + PrivateLink details for EU pilot

Hi Oliver — appreciate the clear checklist. We're aligned on timeline and can deliver a compact evidence pack by EOD Oct 15 (earlier if needed). Quick notes and what's attached: 

- Residency statement: Redwood confirms that Private deployments (customer-managed VPC) provisioned into our EU region will not egress to non-EU regions by default. Any cross-region replication must be explicitly requested and authorized via PO + security review. (See attached: redwood-residency-onboarding-worksheet.xlsx)

- PrivateLink topology: included as a simplified diagram for the staging/onboarding flow (privatelink-topology-diagram.png). It shows the peering endpoint, NAT/egress control plane, and optional transit gateway points.

- CAIQ/SIG subset: we'll provide answers for network segmentation, keystore separation, and key rotation cadence in the SIG workbook you requested. We typically provide a redacted CAIQ snapshot for pre-sales and a full SIG under NDA.

- SOC 2 artifacts: we will point you to our dataroom paths for the encryption and change-control artifacts (I included a HubSpot link for the intake; Marissa will trigger dataroom access once we get your e-sign on the MPA).

- Ephemeral keys and keystore separation: short answer — for Redwood Private we support per-customer keystore partitions. Ephemeral session keys for KV caches are rotated on a per-session basis and are not persisted in a shared keystore. Kimberly and our infra team can provide a short lifecycle diagram and artifact references.

Plan: Marissa will own the dataroom handoff and will follow up with the SIG workbook completion. Kimberly will validate keystore lifecycle statements and provide an artifact pointer. I'll coordinate the packet and send the files by Oct 15.

Attachments:
- redwood-residency-onboarding-worksheet.xlsx (worksheet with declarative answers + ops contacts)
- privatelink-topology-diagram.png (simplified topology)

Next steps: Please confirm whether Veridian needs a signed SOW or a separate MSA addendum for private peering to start provisioning the staging endpoint.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Head of Technical Sales (EMEA)
Redwood Inference

Hi Oliver — attaching the one-page keystore lifecycle note and SOC 2 pointers in the dataroom. To summarize here: 

- Keystore lifecycle (attached): session keys (KV cache) TTL = 12 hours default for staging, configurable down to 1 hour for production; rotated on session termination; per-customer keystore partitions are enforced in Private deployments. No session keys are written to a shared long-term keystore.
- SOC 2 artifacts: dataroom paths provided — encryption_at_rest.pdf (ART-ENCR-2026-03), change_control_log_redacted.zip (CHG-LOG-2026-06). I have created a dataroom task for Marissa to grant Veridian access once the MPA is countersigned.
- PrivateLink topology: added a DR/standby egress swimlane to the diagram and labeled routing ownership (Customer networking owns route policy; Redwood owns endpoint maintenance and egress enforcement for platform-initiated traffic).

I'll upload the one-pager and pointers to the shared Drive and mark the onboarding HubSpot ticket HS-328104 as ready for provisioning.
